content: For accessibility work, this student project prioritizes keyboard navigation, visible focus states, readable contrast, and descriptive labels. No formal accessibility audit has been completed.
The image-classification experiment uses Python and PyTorch. The dataset and evaluation results are not finalized; do not state an accuracy score or sample count.
The student learning community prefers concise monthly updates with a friendly opening, clear headings, and one practical next step. Avoid emojis.
The community workshop is intended for beginners and should feel welcoming. Date, venue, price, registration URL, and capacity have not been decided.

The study-planning app is an early prototype with task lists and local SQLite storage. Offline-first behavior is being explored; no security certification, public release, or external integrations are confirmed.
When writing to project teammates, use a warm, respectful, direct tone and ask for a specific status or blocker rather than a vague update.

The productivity prototype stores local data in SQLite. Cloud synchronization is not implemented, and offline-first design introduces synchronization and conflict-resolution trade-offs if sync is added later.
The study assistant is a prototype for demonstrating task organization and saved study context. It is not a deployed autonomous tutor and should not be described as one.
